name: Input capture
threading: Message thread: arm, startNow, requestStop, discard, take, status, reap. Audio thread: process only (no allocation, locks or I/O). Lifecycle calls from other threads are lock-free handoffs through atomics.
platforms: Any C++17 compiler. No JUCE and no host types.
standalone_test_command: cmake -S modules/input_capture -B build/input_capture && cmake --build build/input_capture && ctest --test-dir build/input_capture
summary: Records the track input into a preallocated buffer: Arm, Capture, Stop, Keep. Synced mode starts on the next bar line and ends by host position (bar-exact through tempo changes); Free mode is a ring that keeps the last N seconds. Output is identical for any host block size.
limits: Mono or stereo, 8 kHz to 384 kHz, at most 60 s, 100 MiB and 11,520,000 frames; synced captures of 1 to 8 bars; synced captures that cannot fit are refused, free ring captures are clamped
adapters: Call `process()` from the audio callback before anything overwrites the input buffer, passing the host transport; poll `status()` and call `reap()` from a UI timer; call `take()` on a worker thread.
adapter_notes: The captured samples are planar floats at the host rate; wrap them in your own source type.
removal: Delete the folder; callers lose live input capture only.
